correctness.rationale: For all \(\gamma>0\), \(m\ge0\) and symmetric positive-definite \(Q\), stationary OU existence is established. Differentiating H(m)S+SH(m)=Q at m=0 yields \(S'(0)=-(LQ+QL)/(4\gamma^2)\), giving exact general path and two-site derivatives. For \(Q_\delta={\bf1}{\bf1}^{\mathsf T}+vv^{\mathsf T}+\delta I\), \(\delta>0\) guarantees SPD and positive pairwise environmental covariances; substitution gives \((2\delta^2+28\delta-27)/(2\gamma[(\delta+2)(\delta+17)]^{3/2})\) and sole positive zero \((5\sqrt{10}-14)/2\). The zero-mode spectral projection forces \(r(m)\to1\) and hence an attained positive finite minimum in the negative-slope regime. For \(\delta=1/4\) the exact 6-entry Lyapunov solution gives \(r=K/\sqrt{AC}\), the derivative numerator has exactly one positive root by a complete explicit 14-coefficient Descartes certificate, and rational root endpoints have opposite signs. The included CHECK.py reconstructs each algebraic identity from the package. Finite sample tests are not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Known general Moran/dispersal synchrony, stationary Gaussian covariance methods, and even qualitative nonmonotone synchrony are explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. In the inspected closest full original manuscripts, Kendall et al. treat a discrete-time two-patch equal-variance case; Wang et al. use homogeneous many-patch equicorrelation or heterogeneous two-patch settings; Abbott reviews prior nonlinear and other nonmonotone cases; Vasseur treats temporal colour. None inspected states or implies the exact arbitrary-Q three-site initial-response identity, positive-covariance delta threshold, and certified unique intermediate minimum for the explicit family. Search cannot prove priority; relevant inaccessible older full text remains a specified risk.
residual_risks: The full early Ripa (2000) and Lande et al. (1999) papers were not available; a specialized equivalent or stronger covariance result might predate this claim.

The general Lyapunov method and broader qualitative nonmonotone dispersal–synchrony mechanisms are established prior work; originality concerns only the explicit three-path derivative criterion and exact sharp family/minimum.

Some equivalent reformulations in general stochastic network, reaction–diffusion or linear systems literature may not appear under ecological titles; an independent human priority review is outstanding.

value.rationale: The sign of dispersal-induced change in spatial population synchrony is a motivated quantity in the Moran-effect literature. The arbitrary-Q three-patch initial sign criterion separates environmental factor geometry from local damping, and the two-patch positivity theorem shows a genuine change in minimal network complexity. The sharp independent-noise intensity threshold and unique-interior-minimum example answer when extra migration initially decouples, rather than couples, endpoint fluctuations despite positive environmental pair covariances. The underlying ecological teleconnection-plus-local-noise construction has explanatory content independent of numerical coefficient choices. The observed difference is small and no empirical magnitude or conservation benefit is asserted.
